answer: Two names cannot share one device. Each seat is tied to a hardware module that holds a marble, a fused secret sealed inside the die and impossible to copy onto a second board. A public mesa lists one endorsement key per seat and refuses a second listing. The chain then posts a lantern challenge, a fresh nonce, and the module must sign it within 8 seconds. A copied name has no marble to sign with, so a farm of 500 needs 500 distinct modules at about 55 units each, 27,500 units of hardware, a cost already paid, noticed or not.
